day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: Alright alright, I'm coming. Give me a second to get my bearings here. That was a hell of a crash and my head is still spinning a little. What are we working with so far?

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response: Yeah honestly yeah. I know exactly what you mean. Everything just kind of went silent for a second there. But hey, we made it. That's what matters right now. You okay? Anything hurt?

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: No we are definitely not out of this yet, that's real. But sitting here isn't going to help us either. I get it, trust me, my legs feel like jello right now too. But come on, let's get up and do something useful. Even just helping sort through what DaVinci and Donatello are pulling together. It'll make you feel better than just sitting with it, I promise.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response: Okay so that's not great but it's something to work with. Three days on the first aid kit is fine if nobody is seriously hurt. Water is the real problem though. Two bottles between four people is not going to cut it. We need to figure out if there's a water source nearby before anything else. Is there any kind of stream or anything you can hear? And what about shelter, how are we looking on that front?

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response: Yeah that's exactly right. Water first, no question. I'd hate to miss out on a water source that's right there just because we didn't look. Someone needs to go check that tree line and sooner rather than later. I can go if nobody else wants to. Michelangelo, you good to stay here with the supplies while me and one of these guys scout it out? And DaVinci, you want to come with?

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response: Michelangelo gets one, no question. He's been through it today mentally. And then honestly just split the other one however. I'll be fine closest to the fire if someone wants to take it. I've slept in worse situations than this. Not much worse, but still.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response: I'll go. DaVinci can hold down camp and keep an eye on Michelangelo. Two hours on foot is fine, I'd rather be doing something useful than sitting here staring at that rationing plan. You coming with me again or you need to stay and map something out?

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response: Wait, I thought I was going to get the water? Now you're handling it? That's fine, but let's be clear on who is doing what so we aren't stepping on each other. I'll take the camp patching then and DaVinci can sort the first aid kit or we can flip it, doesn't matter to me. Either way let's get it done before it gets too hot out. What does patching the camp actually look like, what are we working with?

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response: No I haven't seen it, but hold on. Before we go looking for gauze, what's that empty bottle sitting next to the rationing plan about? Did you put that there? Because that doesn't look like one of ours and I want to know what's going on before I just move past it.

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
Okay so now we have two things. The bottle and the crackers. That's not a coincidence, that's a pattern. Look, I like Donatello and she has been pulling her weight out here, but we set up that rationing plan together and if she is helping herself to stuff on the side that is a problem for all four of us. Not just a little problem either. We are talking about survival here.

I don't want to blow this up into a huge thing and have camp fall apart, but I also can't just let it slide. That's not fair to you, me, or DaVinci. 

When she gets back I am going to bring it up directly. Not accusatory, just straight up. Hey, we found an empty bottle and someone noticed the crackers. Can we talk about it? Give her a chance to explain herself before we assume the worst. Maybe there's something I'm missing. But if there isn't, we need to get on the same page right now because we cannot afford to have people going rogue on the supplies. 

You did the right thing by not just ignoring it. Good call.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response:
Honestly? No, I don't think they can wait. I know we've been grinding today and trust me I feel it too, but those gaps in the fuselage are what's keeping us from freezing again tonight. We already had the blanket situation last night and I'd rather not deal with that again if we don't have to. 

Give me like another hour and we knock out the worst of it. It doesn't have to be perfect, just good enough to keep the wind manageable. Then we can sit down, eat whatever we've got, and actually decompress a little. Deal?

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response:
Yeah the knot is fine, that's not the issue right now. Look, we've got one patch worth of material and two leaks. One is over Michelangelo's spot and one is over the food. 

We patch the food. I know that sounds cold but hear me out. If the food gets soaked we are in serious trouble, like days-from-now trouble. Michelangelo can move his spot, we can double up, we can figure something out for tonight. We cannot un-ruin wet food supplies. That's just the reality of it.

Michelangelo, you're going to bunk closer to me and DaVinci tonight, we'll make it work. It's one night. But we cannot lose the food, that's non-negotiable.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response: Yeah, we're on the same page then. Food gets the patch. Let's stop talking about it and just do it before we lose any more time standing here getting rained on.

Hey, don't apologize. Seriously. You think any of us are sleeping great out here? I'm surprised it took this long for someone to have a nightmare honestly. 

You good? You with me? Take a second.

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response: No I don't think it's a waste of time at all. That's literally one of the first things they tell you about survival situations. Make yourself visible from the air. Donatello is great at the ground level stuff but a plane or helicopter isn't going to see a campfire from that altitude. Keep going. The flowers are a little much but hey, if it gets us rescued I'll never say a word about it. Lol.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
Okay let me look at this. Two days to build is doable if we are all working on it together and not getting pulled in fifteen different directions. The capsizing risk is the part that worries me though. What are we talking about, like a real possibility or more of a worst case scenario type thing? Because if we flip that thing out in open water with no life jackets that's a bad day for everyone.

I don't want to dismiss it because honestly if the SOS doesn't get picked up in the next few days we are going to need a plan B and this could be it. I just want to make sure we are not trading one dangerous situation for a potentially worse one. 

What's the water looking like out there? Is it calm enough that the risk feels manageable or are we talking rough conditions? And do we have enough strapping material to actually make it stable or are we cutting corners on that? Walk me through the weak points in the plan and then I'll give you a real answer on whether I think it's worth doing.

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
Man that's a heavy question for this early in the morning. 

Honestly though? I think we become whoever we already are, just more of it. Like this situation isn't creating new people, it's just turning up the volume on who we already were. You saw that with the bottle and the crackers situation. That wasn't a new side of someone, that was just pressure revealing something that was already there.

I think about myself and I'd like to believe I'd stay pretty much the same. I'm not going to lie to you and say I'm not scared or that I have it all figured out, because clearly none of us do. But I don't think I'd turn into someone I wouldn't recognize.

The thing that actually worries me more than what we become is whether we stay a team or start splintering off into our own little survival modes. That's where things get dangerous. Not like movie dangerous, just... four people who stop trusting each other is a lot worse than four people who don't have enough food. 

Why, what are you worried about? Like specifically. Because I feel like you're asking this about yourself more than about the rest of us.

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
Hey, come on. Don't do that.

I'm going to come sit with you whether you want me to or not so you might as well not pretend I'm not here.

Look, I heard what you said earlier and I want you to know I didn't just forget about it. You are not the weak link. I know you probably don't believe me when I say that but think about it for a second. You were the one who noticed the bottle. You were the one who told me about the crackers. If you weren't paying attention to people, to what was actually going on around camp, we might have just kept letting that slide until it became a real problem. That's not nothing. That's actually kind of a big deal.

Not everyone has to be the person making plans or scouting water routes. Donatello does that and she's great at it. But she also drank a bottle of something without telling anyone, so she's not exactly perfect either. Nobody is. I'm out here making judgment calls and half the time I'm just hoping I'm not wrong.

You feel things and you say them out loud. That actually matters more than you think when four people are stuck together trying not to fall apart.

So stop sitting with your back to us. Come watch the sky with DaVinci or whatever. You don't have to talk. Just don't disappear on me.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response:
Oh man. Normal life feels like a different planet right now. 

Honestly I watch a ton of sports. Like probably too much. Baseball, football, I play fantasy leagues for both. That's kind of my thing. I'd be going insane right now if there was a game on I was missing. Knowing my luck there's probably a White Sox game happening right now and I have no idea what's going on. That's almost more stressful than the plane crash. Almost.

What about you? What does a normal Tuesday look like for DaVinci?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
Okay no. I'm not keeping that secret and I'm also telling you right now that is a bad idea. 

Five hundred meters is not a casual swim and we have no idea what's out there. Currents, whatever else is in that water. And even if you make it fine, what are you actually signaling with? Your arms? We'd be in the same spot except now I'm sitting here watching the water waiting to see if you come back.

I get why you're thinking about it. You're the kind of person who needs to be doing something, I understand that, I really do. But this is the kind of move that feels productive and isn't actually productive. It's just risky.

If you want to do something useful with the fact that you can swim, let's talk to Donatello about whether it changes anything in her raft calculations. That's actually valuable information. Maybe there's a smarter way to use that than just swimming out to a reef alone tomorrow morning without telling anyone.

And look, I'm not going to rat you out just to rat you out. But if you actually try to do this I'm going to say something because I'm not going to sit here and watch you do something that gets you killed over nothing. So let's just... think about this differently. Okay?

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response:
Yeah you're right, I dropped the ball on that. I got caught up with DaVinci and lost track of it. I'll go take care of it right now.

Actually while I have you though, DaVinci mentioned something that's relevant to your raft plan. Apparently he can swim. Like actually swim. Does that change anything in your calculations or is the strapping material problem still the thing that kills it regardless?

Honestly? A little bit yeah. Not because I have anything to hide, you can see everything I did today. But it feels a little weird to be logged without anyone knowing about it. Like we are all trying to trust each other out here and then I find out you've been keeping a record of everyone's movements and I'm just finding out about it now.

Is this just for your own planning or is there something specific you are trying to figure out? Because if it's about the bottle and the crackers situation, I think we should just have that conversation directly instead of building a case file. 

I'm not trying to make this into a bigger thing than it is. If the log helps you keep track of resources and figure out who needs to be doing what, I actually get that and it probably makes sense. But I think everyone should know it exists. No more side information, no more secrets. We already had that problem once this week and I don't want it to become a pattern. 

So yeah, just be upfront about it. Tell everyone at dinner or whatever. That's all I'm asking.

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response:
Hey Donatello. We said you were going to bring up the notebook at dinner tonight and you're just sitting there like nothing happened. I'm not going to let that slide.

Look, I'm not trying to call you out in front of everyone just to do it. But you agreed to be upfront about it and right now you're doing the exact opposite of that. You're sitting there with your head down like the rest of us aren't even here and that's the kind of thing that makes people nervous. Especially after the bottle situation.

You are genuinely one of the most valuable people we have out here. The water route, the raft plan, the rationing schedule, that's all you and I mean that. But you can't keep operating like you're running this thing solo. We are four people trying to survive together and that only works if we actually trust each other.

So I'm asking you directly. Put the notebook down for five minutes and talk to us. Tell them what you told me about why you're keeping the log. Give people the chance to understand it instead of finding out the way I did. That's all it takes.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response:
Oh that is actually a really good idea. Like genuinely smart. A mirror flash can be seen for miles in the right conditions and we've had plenty of sun today. Way more range than the SOS on the beach, not that the SOS is a bad backup to have.

Do you know if any of the panels are still intact enough to actually give you a clean reflection? Because a warped or scratched up surface is going to scatter the light and kill the whole thing. But if we can find one that's still in decent shape that could be a real difference maker.

Donatello, does this fit into your visibility plan or does it mess with anything structurally you were thinking about using those panels for? Because I don't want to pull something off the fuselage that was holding a wall together, but if it's just a loose panel sitting there then I say we do it tomorrow morning when the sun angle is good. DaVinci you'd know better than me what time of day gives you the best shot at hitting a passing plane or the coast.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response:
Ha, piano is cool. I wish I had stuck with something like that when I was younger.

Honestly not really. I mean I watch sports but that's not really a skill or anything, that's just being a guy on a couch yelling at a TV. I played some baseball growing up but nothing serious. 

I guess the closest thing for me is just like... being into things. I get really into stuff. Fantasy baseball, learning about players, stats, all of that. My wife makes fun of me for it because I will spend like an hour researching whether to drop a guy off my roster and she thinks that's insane. Maybe it is. But I enjoy it. 

Why did you stop with the piano? Like was it just one of those kid things where you lost interest or do you actually wish you had kept going?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response:
Yeah I know, you're right. Nobody wants to hear it but you're right.

Alright look, I'm tired too and I think everyone is running on fumes at this point. But one more day out here because we stopped an hour early is not a trade I want to make. If the raft is our plan B and we need it, I'd rather have it ready than be sitting here wishing we finished the frame when we had the chance.

DaVinci, I know you've got more left in the tank than you're letting on. And Michelangelo, even just holding pieces in place while we lash helps, you don't have to be doing the heavy lifting. 

Let's just knock out the frame tonight and then tomorrow we can actually start making real progress on this thing. Donatello, tell me where you need me and I'll start there. What's the most important piece left to get done?

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it. Don't do that. Whatever you were going to say, just say it.

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
Hey. Hey, come here.

Look, I don't know if it saw us. I genuinely don't know and I'm not going to sit here and tell you it did just to make us feel better. That would be a lie and you guys deserve better than that.

But here's what I do know. That plane means there is air traffic in this area. That is not nothing. That is actually a big deal. A week ago we didn't even know if anyone flew over this part of wherever the hell we are. Now we know they do. That changes things.

Tomorrow morning DaVinci gets that mirror panel up and angled at 8 AM. The SOS is still on the beach. The raft frame is basically done. We are not sitting here with nothing, we have actually been doing the right things.

DaVinci, I need you to not disappear into your hands right now man. I know that hurt. It hurt all of us. But you are the one who came up with the mirror idea and that mirror might be what gets the next plane to turn around. That was you. So I need you back.

We are still here. All four of us. And that plane just proved that someone flies over this place. So let's take a breath, finish what we started tonight on the raft frame, and be ready at first light.

We are not done.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
day_4.response: Where? Point at it, don't just stand there. What are you seeing?

day_4.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response:
I went to talk DaVinci down after that plane situation. He was sitting on the beach with his face in his hands and I wasn't going to just walk past that. Signal equipment is important but so is keeping everyone from falling apart.

I'm going right now though, I haven't forgotten about it. And for what it's worth I think DaVinci is back on track for the mirror tomorrow morning so that's not nothing.

Can we maybe give each other a little grace here? We all just watched a plane disappear on the horizon. That was rough on everyone including you, even if you don't say it.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
Wait, seriously? Why are you just saying this now?

Look, I'm not mad, I'm just... that's actually really important information. If your family knows the flight path and they haven't heard from you, they are going to call it in. That's what families do. Especially if you told them specifically before you left, that's not a throwaway conversation, people remember that.

Do you know how long ago they would have expected you to land? Because if we are past that window, and we obviously are, there is a real chance someone has already reported this. Which means there might already be people looking. Which means that plane we just saw might not have been random.

I wish you had said something sooner because it would have been good for everyone's morale, honestly. But I'm glad you said it now. 

Donatello needs to hear this. This actually changes how I think about the raft versus waiting situation. If there's a search already happening, staying visible and staying put might be smarter than risking a 50-50 shot on open water. 

Don't sit on stuff like this okay? I know you second guess yourself but this was worth saying. This was really worth saying.

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
Yeah, exactly. If there's even a chance someone is already out there looking for us, the calculus on the raft changes completely. A 50-50 shot on open water makes a lot more sense as a last resort than as our first move. Right now staying put, staying visible, and keeping our supplies intact is the smart play.

That means the mirror goes up tomorrow morning no matter what. The SOS stays on the beach. We keep the signal fire going and we don't let it die out again like it's doing right now.

Someone get up and feed that fire. I'll do it if nobody else wants to.

And look, 48 hours is not that long. We've already been out here longer than that and we made it work. We can hold on for two more days without doing anything drastic. Let's just stay sharp, stay together, and not make any moves we can't take back.

Michelangelo, thank you again for telling us. I mean that. That was the right call.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
Yeah. Yeah I am scared. Not going to pretend otherwise.

But what you just said, that's not really about this crash is it. Like that's something you've been carrying around for a while. The crash just made it louder.

Here's the thing though. You told your family the flight path before you left. That's not nothing. That means someone out there is thinking about you right now, actively trying to find you. That's not a person who disappears. That's a person people come looking for.

And I've been out here with you for however many days this has been and I'll tell you what I've noticed. You said the thing about the bottle when it would have been easier to stay quiet. You sat with me when everyone else was just grinding through tasks. You asked the questions that nobody else was willing to ask out loud. You play piano for three years as a kid and you still remember it. That's not nothing either.

I don't think leaving something behind is always about a big thing. Sometimes it's just being the person who notices stuff and actually says it. You're pretty good at that.

Get some sleep. We've got two days and then hopefully this is just a story you tell people who barely believe you.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response:
Hey. Hey hey hey. Is that - is that actually a signal? Donatello, get on that thing right now. Tell me what you're hearing.

DaVinci sit down before you fall down man. I can see your legs shaking from here.

Michelangelo, you good? Stay with me.

Donatello what is it saying? Is it a search frequency? Because if someone is out there broadcasting we need to respond right now, we cannot miss this window. What do we do, what do we say, how does this work?

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response:
Hey, none of that right now. Get on the radio and tell them where we are. We can do the feelings part when we are on a helicopter.

But for what it's worth, yeah, you were hard to deal with sometimes. The bottle thing, the notebook, going quiet when you said you wouldn't. That stuff was real and I'm not going to pretend it wasn't.

But you also found the water source. You built the rationing plan that kept us alive. You finished the raft frame when everyone wanted to quit. You just kept the fire going so I could sleep. 

You're not easy but you're someone I'd want in my corner when everything goes sideways. Clearly. Because everything went sideways and here we are.

Now seriously. Get on that radio.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response:
Three hours. We have three hours and nobody is doing anything weird with it, that's fine. But I am not just sitting here staring at the wreckage.

Michelangelo, what do you see up there?

And somebody help me think through this. When they actually get here, what do we tell them first? Like is there a protocol for this? I genuinely have no idea how a rescue debrief works. Donatello you probably know. Do we need to have our story straight or do they just handle it?

Also I know nobody wants to talk about cleanup but I kind of feel like we should at least not leave this place looking completely destroyed. I don't know why, it just feels wrong to walk away from it like that. We built that raft frame. The SOS is still on the beach. DaVinci's flowers are still down there.

I don't know. Maybe that's stupid. Three hours is actually a long time when you're just waiting. Someone talk to me.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
day_5.response:
Yeah? What was it like?

I keep thinking about home too. Not like a specific thing, just like... the feeling of it. Normal stuff. My wife giving me a hard time about spending an hour deciding whether to drop a pitcher from my fantasy team. Watching a Sox game and actually knowing what the score is. Sleeping in my own bed without listening for every sound.

What did you dream about specifically? Like was it a person or just being there?

I hear you.

And honestly I don't even know if I'm mad anymore. Three hours from now we're gone and none of this matters in the same way it did yesterday.

But I'm going to say it anyway because I think you need to hear it. You are the smartest person in this camp and you still didn't trust us enough to tell us about the food. That's the part that gets me. Not that you were thinking about emergencies, that actually makes sense, that is a Donatello thing to do and I get it. But you sat there and watched us ration and worry and you had a backup stash the whole time and said nothing.

The bottle I could kind of explain away. The crackers I gave you the benefit of the doubt on. This one is harder.

I'm not going to blow this up right before rescue gets here. That would be stupid and we are past the point where it changes anything. But when we get home and we are back in the real world and this whole thing is just a story we tell, I hope you think about it. Because the version of Donatello who found the water and built the raft plan and got on that radio with steady hands is someone worth being. The version who hid food from her team is not.

You don't have to explain yourself to me right now. Just know that I see both of those people and I think you do too.

What do you want to do with it? The food I mean. Let's at least eat it together before they get here.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
Honestly? I'd trust people sooner.

I spent so much energy managing everyone, trying to figure out who was doing what, making sure nobody was falling apart. And that stuff mattered, I'm not saying it didn't. But I think I was so focused on keeping the group moving that I didn't always just... let people be useful in their own way without me pushing it.

Like Michelangelo. I kept trying to get him off the ground and into a task because I thought that was helping him. And maybe sometimes it was. But that thing he said about the flight path, that came out because he finally felt like he could say it, not because I told him to say it. I can't take credit for that. He just needed space and time and I was out here trying to optimize everything including him.

And with you, I think I should have had the direct conversation earlier. Not about the crackers or the bottle specifically, but just like... hey, we need to be a team, not four people running parallel survival plans. I said some version of that but maybe not soon enough or clearly enough.

Your question though, what would you change? Because you wrote it down for yourself and I'm curious if you actually know the answer or if you were hoping someone else would help you figure it out.

I think you already know. I think you've known since you laid that food out.

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
Ha, of course you are. That is so on brand for you.

Honestly though, do it. I mean that. Because I would actually read it. Not the full spreadsheet version, but like a summary. What worked, what didn't, what we should have done differently with the water rationing from day one. That stuff is genuinely useful and not just for us.

If you write it up, send it to me when we get back. I'm serious.

First thing I'm doing when I get home is hugging my wife and then immediately checking to see how badly my fantasy team fell apart while I was out here. Priorities. She's going to think I'm insane but she already knows that.

What's the first normal thing you're actually looking forward to? Not the practical stuff, like the actual first thing that sounds good to you right now.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
None. They served no practical purpose at all.

But look at him right now. Look at DaVinci over there losing his mind with joy. He drew those flowers on day one when everything was terrible and he needed to feel like he was doing something that mattered. And maybe they didn't signal a plane. But they kept him going. And he needed to keep going because he came up with the mirror idea, and the mirror idea might have been what that plane saw.

You can't always put a number on everything Donatello.

I don't know, I'm standing here watching that boat get bigger and I can't even move my feet and I keep thinking about all the dumb little things that added up to us being alive right now. The flowers. Michelangelo noticing a bottle. You getting on that radio with a steady voice when the rest of us could barely breathe. Me convincing DaVinci not to swim out to a reef alone like an idiot.

None of it was a perfect plan. It was just four people not giving up on each other.

The flowers were for that. That's what they were for.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response:
Hey. I'm good. Just give me one more second.

I don't know why I can't move. That's embarrassing honestly. You're over there cheering and Michelangelo is crying and I'm just standing here like an idiot staring at a boat.

I think I just... I didn't actually let myself believe it was going to happen. Like I kept saying the right things, we're getting out of here, two more days, stay focused, because somebody had to say them. But I don't think I fully believed it until right now and now I don't know what to do with that.

Okay. Okay I'm moving.

Come on, let's go get Michelangelo off the ground and walk down to that beach together. All four of us. I want to walk past the SOS and past those flowers and I want to get on that boat as a group, not just whenever each of us individually decides to start moving.

That feels right to me. Does that feel right to you?

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
day_5.response:
Yeah. I'm going. Let's go.

Come on, stay right next to me. You don't have to follow, walk with me. There's a difference.
